narrative: Each panel represents one dimension of the sovereign investment template as documented across all five cases. Read left to right: corporate winners are named and quantified in Panel 1; community promises and their documented gaps occupy Panel 2; regulatory instruments that made the transfers possible fill Panel 3; and residual costs left entirely on the public are logged in Panel 4. Every item derives from official documents, government announcements, or peer-reviewed case studies — nothing is inferred. The consistent pattern is that concentrated corporate benefit is identifiable before the announcement lands, while community promises are calibrated for political communication, not legal enforcement.
why_this_perspective: Executives need a single surface that names who won and who lost in each documented case before any government counterpart deploys the same playbook on them. The evidential level grounds every cell in official documents, dollar amounts, and named firms.
claimed_territory: Concrete documented gains and losses for each named actor — corporations, communities, and states — across all five cases

perspective: How government vocabulary moves a deal from announcement to capture
title: The Sovereign Investment Vocabulary: Six Terms, Three Stages, One Outcome

regions.label: STAGE 1 — FOUNDATION: Licensing and Foreclosing
regions.note: Terms that authorise state action and remove opposition before scrutiny begins

nodes.label: National Security
nodes.definition: Legal construct that converts a discretionary subsidy into a categorical necessity, licensing all downstream regulatory accommodation

nodes.label: National Interest
nodes.definition: Reframes corporate benefit as general public good; makes opposition appear unpatriotic rather than legitimate

nodes.label: Bipartisan Consensus
nodes.definition: Cross-party agreement achieved within hours; forecloses parliamentary scrutiny before affected communities can organise

nodes.label: Whole-of-Government Approach
nodes.definition: Suppresses inter-agency friction — environmental, planning, and labour agencies subordinated to the overriding investment frame

regions.label: STAGE 2 — RECLASSIFICATION: Elaborating and Designating
regions.note: Terms that convert commercial activity into national projects and name the chosen corporate beneficiaries

nodes.label: Modernisation / Digital Transformation
nodes.definition: Reframes corporate expansion as a public upgrade; stigmatises opponents as reactionary laggards before opposition forms

nodes.label: Technological Sovereignty
nodes.definition: Incorporates start-ups and VC firms into the security nexus; reclassifies profit-seeking as sovereign capability provision

nodes.label: Strategic Investment / Strategic Asset
nodes.definition: Legal designation granting named firms preferential treatment — fast-tracked permits, rezoning, reduced employment thresholds — unavailable to rivals

nodes.label: De-risking
nodes.definition: Legitimises selective exclusion of specific firms or countries while maintaining appearance of continued market openness

nodes.label: National Champion
nodes.definition: Corporate entity whose commercial interests are formally reclassified as state interests, locking in monopoly over strategic resources

regions.label: STAGE 3 — DEFENCE: Closing and Bridging
regions.note: Terms that neutralise opposition and construct the legal bridge from announcement to concentrated benefit

nodes.label: Jobs and Skills
nodes.definition: Quantified community promise (300 jobs, 100,000 trained) designed for political communication, not legal enforcement; documented gap in every case

nodes.label: Community Benefit
nodes.definition: Defensive claim that concentrated corporate gains serve everyone; consistently over-stated and under-enforced across all five documented cases

nodes.label: Fast-Track Approval
nodes.definition: Regulatory bridge converting announcement into corporate benefit; compresses environmental review, planning consultation, and competition assessment

nodes.label: Strategic Partnership
nodes.definition: Language that conceals a dependency relationship running in both directions; conditions embedded here outlast the accommodation that comes with them

bridges.label: Once licensed, commercial activity is reclassified as national project
Corporate designation requires defensive legitimation to close opposition

side_boxes.label: EXECUTIVE SIGNALS: What Each Term Means in Practice
items: National security applied to your sector: data-sharing, pricing, or content conditions will follow the accommodation
Bipartisan or whole-of-government language: due-diligence windows are about to compress; normal scrutiny will not protect you
Modernisation or transformation narrative applied to your brand: proprietary lock-in and training mandates will be attached
Strategic designation offered: competitive moat now; state-imposed sourcing or pricing conditions later under the same label
Jobs or community benefit request: government needs a public-facing number; what you sign is political cover, not a binding contract
Strategic partnership proposed: you are being asked to absorb risk and legitimise an outcome already structured for someone else

side_boxes.label: DOCUMENTED CASES WHERE TERMS WERE DEPLOYED
items: National security: SeaMeWe-6 US intervention; AUKUS announcement; France Seabed Warfare Strategy 2022
Modernisation: Greece 2.0 national recovery plan; Microsoft GR for GRowth October 2020
Strategic investment: Greek Laws 4759/2020 and 4864/2021; APE acquisition mandate for ASN
Bipartisan: Labor backs AUKUS within 24 hours; Greek Strategic Investments framework built across ND and Syriza governments
Jobs and skills: 300 jobs over ten years Greece; 100,000 trained by 2025 Greece; Australian jobs resilience framing
De-risking: US pressure on Vietnam and Morocco to screen nickel, EV battery, and electronics investment

narrative: The map is organised into three regions that correspond to the three stages of the sovereign investment template: Stage 1 sets the foundation by licensing state action through security and consensus language; Stage 2 reclassifies corporate activity as public benefit and names the chosen beneficiaries; Stage 3 deploys defensive vocabulary to close off opposition. Arrows show how each term enables or constrains the next. The side box translates each term into a practical signal for executives. A reader moving left to right traces the sequence a government counterpart is actually running — so that when a term appears in a meeting, its downstream consequences are already visible.
why_this_perspective: The five cases share not just a pattern of outcomes but a shared vocabulary that executes the pattern. A framework map that labels each term's argumentative function — foundational, reclassifying, foreclosing, bridging, defensive — gives executives a decoder they can apply in any future negotiation, regardless of sector.
claimed_territory: The conceptual architecture of national-interest language — what each term does argumentatively and what it signals to executives

anchors.label: National security licenses downstream regulatory accommodation
anchors.quote: national security and public order are mobilised to block transactions or shape the conditions under which they happen — not neutral descriptions of threat but instruments that convert discretionary policy choices into apparent categorical necessities.

anchors.label: Bipartisan consensus forecloses parliamentary scrutiny
anchors.quote: within 24 hours of Morrison's AUKUS announcement, Albanese declared Labor backed it — opposition became politically unspeakable.

anchors.label: Modernisation stigmatises opposition as reactionary laggards
anchors.quote: this discourse creates a chasm between those who endorse these changes, the moderns, and those who do not, the laggards — stigmatising opposition as reactionary before it can be organised.

anchors.label: Strategic designation grants preferential regulatory treatment
anchors.quote: Regulatory controls rearticulate the interests of particular politico-economic groups as general interests.

anchors.label: Jobs promise designed for legitimation, not delivery
anchors.quote: The community promise is the template's defensive element. It exists to close the argument that concentrated corporate benefits serve only shareholders. But across all five cases, the promise is structurally designed for legitimation, not delivery.

anchors.label: Fast-tracking compresses due-diligence windows
anchors.quote: Inter-agency friction disappears — timelines accelerate but so do conditions attached; due-diligence windows compress.

anchors.label: Geopolitical fetishism conceals class relations beneath security framing
anchors.quote: geopolitical fetishism privileges geopolitical contestation over the underlying social and class relations of capitalist transformation.

anchors.label: Pathological symbiosis: partnership language conceals dependency
anchors.quote: the language of partnership conceals a dependency relationship that runs in both directions.

anchors.label: Being labelled strategic is a moat that later becomes a constraint
anchors.quote: Being designated strategic is a competitive moat — but it also means the state can later impose conditions citing the same designation.

anchors.label: Clean tech and luxury face the same expanding screening logic
anchors.quote: clean tech and renewables are already identified in many investment-screening national legislations as core technologies to be protected.
